procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade processes the application and issues the certificate.
The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry.
The Indian importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years.

caveats.note: Duty estimate is on Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The origin result is based on the exporter's own declaration of operations and final manufacture.
The '+' in the rule is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is from secondary sources, not the official text.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
